# NekoC

> NekoC compiles a subset of TypeScript into Codemao Kitten N works (`.bcmkn`, block projects) and runs Kitten N / Kitten 4 works headlessly. One `.nk.ts` file can declare the stage, sprites, costumes and all logic. Write plain TS; the compiler turns it into official blocks that open in the Kitten N editor.

## Workflow for AI agents

1. Write `game.nk.ts`.
2. `nekoc check game.nk.ts --json` — type check (against `ts/nekoc.d.ts`), Kitten N compatibility check, project structure check. Writes nothing. Exit code 1 on errors. Each diagnostic: `{severity, source: "syntax"|"types"|"compat"|"project", code, message, file, line, column}`. Fix and re-run until `{"ok": true}`.
3. `nekoc build game.nk.ts` → `game.bcmkn` next to the source (`-o` to change). No template needed.
4. `nekoc run game.bcmkn --ticks 120` — headless run, 60 ticks per second, prints a JSON snapshot (`logs` holds `console.log` output, plus variables, lists, actors). Add `--event key-down:space` or `--event click:100,200` to simulate input.
5. Optional, needs Playwright: `node tools/editor-compat.mjs game.bcmkn` loads the work in the official online editor; `ok: true` means it opens cleanly.
6. Optional: `nekoc test game.nk.ts` runs `test(...)` blocks at compile time.

Kitten 4 target: use `nekoc check game.ts --target kitten4 --json`, then `nekoc compile-ts-kitten4 game.ts --out game.bcm`. Ordinary C-style for loops use generic assignments/live conditions/steps (not KN traverse blocks); continue executes the step, break skips it. Reentrant onMessage/onKey/when for loops are rejected until native per-invocation storage exists. forRange and new custom procedures remain unsupported. No frame-by-frame equivalence to KN traversal is promised. See docs/kitten4.md. Frontend compileFile(entry, host, {target:"kitten4"}) and checkFile(entry, {host, target:"kitten4"}) accept the same target; the browser/Node package compile/check options also expose it, returning canonical bcmkn rather than native bcm.

## A complete file

```ts
const CAT = "https://creation.bcmcdn.com/922/user-files/d2ViXzIwMDJfMTc5ODgyNTlfMzIwOTgxODA1XzE3ODI2MjI4MDAwMDBfRnR3U0xVSjFuU2lkN29neWstTmlzR1hPeHlNYw==.png";

stage({ name: "catch", backdrop: "https://static.codemao.cn/neko/img_stage_defult_portrait.png" });

let score = 0;            // top-level let/const = global variable

function bonus(level: number): number {
  return level * 10;      // small functions inline; costly expansion / recursion uses custom blocks
}

sprite("cat", {
  costumes: [{ name: "idle", url: CAT, centerX: 64, centerY: 64 }],
  x: 0, y: -150, scale: 80,
}, (self) => {
  self.onStart(() => {
    forever(() => {
      if (keyPressed("left")) self.changeX(-8);
      if (keyPressed("right")) self.changeX(8);
      wait(0.02);
    });
  });
  onMessage("hit", () => {
    score += bonus(2);
    self.say(`score ${score}`, 1);
  });
});

onStart(() => {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    wait(1);
    broadcastAndWait("hit");   // broadcast() would not wait for the handlers
  }
  console.log(score);          // 60 (nekoc run --ticks 480)
});
```

## Stage declaration

- `stage({ name?, backdrop? })` — stage name and background URL.
- `sprite(name, options, (self) => { ... })` — creates an actor. Options: `costume` (one URL) or `costumes` (array of URL strings or `{ name?, url, centerX?, centerY? }`; first one is the start costume; unnamed ones become `name`, `name2`, …; names unique), `centerX`, `centerY`, `x`, `y`, `scale` (percent), `rotation` (degrees), `visible`.
- `screen(name, { backdrop }, () => { sprite(...) })` — extra screens; switch with `switchScreen(name)`.
- Resource strings must be string literals or top-level `const` string literals.
- Inside a sprite body, event and action calls belong to that sprite. `self.xxx(...)` is the same as `xxx(...)` there (`self.onStart`, `self.changeX`, `self.nextStyle`, `self.say`, `self.stop`, …).
- Stage coordinates: center is (0, 0), x right, y up; default stage is 900×562 (landscape).

## Supported TypeScript

- `let`/`const`, numbers, strings, booleans, template literals, arrays (`a[i]`, `a[i] = v`, `a.length`, `push`, `includes`, `map`, `filter`, `forEach`, `reduce`, `find`, `findIndex`, `some`, `every`, `sort`, `indexOf`, `join`, `concat`, `slice`, `reverse`, `pop`, `shift`, `unshift`, `splice`), array destructuring.
- Array `push/unshift` and statement `splice` save the receiver and every argument once, left to right, before mutation (also across recursion). `includes/indexOf/lastIndexOf` support numeric `fromIndex`, including negatives and fractional truncation; omit optional undefined arguments. `concat` accepts zero or more statically known arrays/scalars and shallow-copies references. Array callbacks snapshot initial length while ordinary `for...of` observes growth. `filter/forEach/reduce/some/every` skip removed trailing positions; `map/find/findIndex` conservatively reject shrinking or yielding/dispatching callbacks (including indirect calls): move removals after traversal or use an explicit loop. Array spread, thisArg and unsupported extra arguments are compile errors. See docs/api.md for boundaries.
- Statement `splice` normalizes numeric start/deleteCount against length read after all arguments: truncate fractions toward zero, count negative starts from the end, clamp once before mutation, NaN as zero, infinities at boundaries, negative deleteCount as zero, omitted deleteCount through the end. Inserted references keep order and identity; deleted-items return values and sparse arrays remain unsupported.
- Array `slice(start?, end?)` saves the receiver and numeric arguments once in order, then reads length. Fractions truncate toward zero, NaN means zero, negatives count from the end, and ±Infinity/out-of-range bounds clamp to the valid range. Omitted bounds mean zero/length; empty/reversed ranges return a new empty list. Copies are shallow and preserve element reference identity. Omit explicit undefined; non-numeric/null boundaries are errors. Ordinary out-of-bounds reads and sparse-array restrictions are unchanged.
- Strings: `.length`, `s[i]`, `charAt`, `slice`, `substring`, `includes`, `split`, `indexOf`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `replace`, `replaceAll`, `trim`, `repeat`, `padStart`, `padEnd`, `toUpperCase`, `toLowerCase`.
- String charAt/substring and search/split receivers/arguments evaluate once in order. substring clamps/truncates and swaps reversed bounds (equal = empty); slice keeps separate constant/negative-index semantics. Search methods accept numeric optional positions; split accepts uint32 limit and returns a fresh array. Extra/spread/undefined arguments and regex overloads are errors. Dynamic repeat/padding counts, lengths and fill strings are supported with runtime caps of 65536 UTF-16 result/target units. NaN means zero; dynamic negative/infinite repeat counts return empty, invalid constant counts are compile errors. Padding never truncates its source; empty fill is a no-op. Non-BMP partial-fill padding conservatively returns its source. See docs/api.md#typescript-strings for known differences.
- Code-unit selection/search uses BMP proof as a fast path; unknown parameters/containers/rewritten variables compile with a runtime guard, preserving ASCII/Chinese behavior. On these guarded paths non-BMP receivers become empty text to avoid isolated-surrogate VM failures. Native includes(search)/startsWith(search) without position and split(nonemptyLiteralSeparator, limit?) preserve full emoji. Empty/unknown separators use the guard. Names such as self and any/as assertions do not bypass runtime growth safety.
- `Math.floor/ceil/round/trunc/abs/sqrt/exp/log/log10/pow/max/min/random/sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/PI` (radians, like JS).
- Numeric bitwise `& | ^ ~ << >> >>>` and standalone `&= |= ^= <<= >>= >>>=` follow JS int32/uint32 semantics (fractions truncate, NaN/Infinity become 0, shift counts use low 5 bits). Operands evaluate once. Constants fold; conversions/masks/shifts use arithmetic, general `& | ^` use at most 32 warp iterations in share-compatible custom blocks. Use numeric types and split assignment values into statements.
- `if/else`, `while`, `do/while`, C-style `for`, `for...of`, `switch`, `break`, `continue`, labels, ternary, `??`, `try/catch` with `throw`.
- Functions: declarations, default parameters, recursion (custom blocks), `import`/`export` between project files, enums. All explicit arguments (including unused ones) evaluate left to right before omitted/explicit-undefined defaults, which run in parameter order; saved values are per-call references, not clones. Parameter-reading dynamic defaults and unsafe call-site bindings remain unsupported. Small simple functions inline; explicitly numeric static functions with costly call-graph expansion use shared, named custom blocks with per-call frames (docs/ts-inline-budget.md). This bounds generated graphs, not execution time. Types, interfaces, `as`, `!`, `satisfies` are stripped.
- `console.log(x)` writes to the run log.
- Plain data objects: `{ x: 1, nested: { n: 2 } }`, `p.x`, `p["x"]` (or a literal-typed `const` key), `p.x += 1`, standalone `p.x++`. Compiled as opaque numeric references into a hidden list heap, never `_object_*` blocks, for the official share player. Aliases, nested objects, objects in arrays, function parameters/returns and root timer mutations share identity. Initialize every non-optional property in a literal (omitted `x?:` properties read `undefined`); dynamic/undeclared keys, object coercion/logging/JSON, delete, and value-producing property updates are errors. Log scalar properties instead. Object programs use custom procedures to evaluate function arguments once; recursive object mutation/allocation or recursive locals are rejected. Heap storage is reclaimed on restart, not per allocation. Details/evidence: docs/ts-share-objects.md.
- Top-level statements run at startup in source order; `onStart` handlers start after them and run concurrently.
- Timers: `setTimeout(cb, ms)`, `setInterval(cb, ms)`, `clearTimeout(h)`, `clearInterval(h)` (frame-quantized, root workspace only, callbacks cannot capture function parameters).
- Also `Math.sign/cbrt/log2/hypot/atan2`, `Number.isInteger`, `Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => …)`, `Array(n).fill(v)`.
- Classes (stages 1 and 2): top-level class declarations, initialized fields, constructors and parameter properties, `new`, instance methods and `this`. Instances use the same opaque heap handles as plain objects; methods receive the handle once as their first parameter and use per-call frames for recursion. Single inheritance, super, abstract members, instanceof narrowing, virtual method/accessor dispatch and explicit-class static fields/methods are supported. The checker must resolve a class or base receiver. Fields without initializers must be assigned before every constructor exit unless they are optional (`x?: T`) or typed with `null`/`undefined`, which start as `undefined`; incomplete `this` escapes are rejected. See docs/ts-classes.md for initialization order and boundaries.
- null/undefined (docs/ts-nullable.md): values whose type spells out `null`/`undefined` (`T | null`, `x?: T`, `next: Node | null = null`) hold runtime sentinels (text `"null"`/`"undefined"` for numbers, booleans, arrays and references; numbers -1/-2 for strings), so linked lists, trees and optional config objects work. Supported: `a?.b`, `a?.b.c`, `a?.[i]`, `a?.m()` (receiver evaluated once, nothing evaluated after a short-circuit), `a ?? b`, standalone `a ??= b`, `=== null`, `!== undefined`, `== null`, `if (x)` and checker narrowing. Printing and string concatenation show `null`/`undefined` like JS. Errors: null arithmetic/relational comparisons, using a maybe-null value without narrowing, `x!` on maybe-null values, `?.` on call results, `f?.()`, `??=` as an expression, mixed unions like `string | number | null`, nulls in `any`/`unknown`, `pop`/`shift`/`find` results used as undefined, `delete`.
- Map/Set (docs/ts-map-set.md): string/number keys, including literal unions; Map set/get/has/delete/clear/size, Set add/has/delete/clear/size, literal Map entries and array Set initializers. References preserve alias identity through parameters/returns and fields; cross-file use requires explicit signatures and caller collection annotations. Get returns V | undefined and supports ?? or explicit narrowing; immediate if(m.has(k)) m.get(k)! is accepted with a conservative no-intervening-call/write/property-read rule. Direct for-of keys/values/entries and inline forEach preserve insertion order and JS live mutation semantics. forEach callback var declarations are rejected; use explicitly initialized let/const locals. Optional collection method calls are rejected; save the receiver, check undefined/null, then evaluate arguments and call inside the branch (?.size is supported). SameValueZero keys include NaN and signed zero. Values may be scalars or object/class/collection handles; array values, nullable/mixed-domain values, escaping iterators, Array.from(iterators), spread, WeakMap/WeakSet and object keys are errors. Hidden heap storage grows with historical insertions; use small collections.
- Not supported (compile errors): mixin/builtin inheritance, static this/inheritance/blocks/accessors, #private fields, index signatures, class expressions/decorators, method values/bind/call/apply, this-capturing closures across yields, object methods/getters/spread, object destructuring, `new Date/Promise`, closures as values, `in`, `f?.()`, `JSON`, generators, `async` functions/callbacks, `await` expressions and `for await...of`. Values are numbers, strings, booleans, lists, plain objects, class instances and Map/Set references.
- No Promise or microtask semantics: async/await is rejected on the original AST (including unused/nested functions and imports), with file/line/column diagnostics, even with `--no-types` and in npm/browser frontends. For synchronous-only code, remove async/await and use ordinary functions. Use `wait(seconds)` for cooperative delays or an explicit event state machine for asynchronous sequencing; neither reproduces JS Promise/microtask ordering.

## Events

`onStart(body)`, `onClick(body)` (sprite clicked), `onKey(key, state?, body)` (`"space"`, `"up"`, `"a"`…; state `"down"`/`"up"`), `onMessage(message, body)`, `when(condition, body)`, `onBumpActor(target, body)`.

## Control

`wait(seconds)`, `waitUntil(cond)`, `forever(body)`, `repeatTimes(n, body)`, `repeatUntil(cond, body)`, `forRange(name, from, to, step, body)`, `breakLoop()`, `stop(option?)` (no argument: this script; `"0"`: everything), `restart()`, `warp(body)` (run without frame yields), `broadcast(message, value?)`, `broadcastAndWait(message)`, `switchScreen(name)`.

Kitten N `deleteClone()`/`self.deleteClone()` and `restart()` have no physical next socket: end their block stack with them. Direct following statements (also after inline expansion) produce `NEKOC_TERMINAL_NEXT` with a source location and rewrite hint. An explicit branch/loop/procedure may end with either while its enclosing container/call retains a legal continuation. Deleting an original actor can continue there; deleting a clone cancels its tasks; restart resets the work. No code is silently discarded. `stop` retains its next socket and dynamic scope. Existing works with illegal next edges fail `nekoc check` as `terminal_block_has_next`.

## Sprite actions

Motion: `moveSteps(n)`, `moveTo(x, y)`, `setX(x)`, `setY(y)`, `changeX(dx)`, `changeY(dy)`, `glideTo(x, y, seconds)`, `turn(deg)`, `pointTowards(deg)`, `faceTo(target)`, `bounceOffEdge()`, `setRotationType(type)`.
Looks: `show()`, `hide()`, `say(text, seconds?)` (with seconds the script waits), `ask(text)` + `answer()`, `setScale(p)`, `changeScale(d)`, `nextStyle()`, `setStyle(nameOrIndex)`, `setEffect(name, v)`, `changeEffect(name, d)`, `clearEffects()`, `setLayer(...)`.
Pen: `penDown()`, `penUp()`, `setPenColor(color)`, `setPenSize(n)`, `clearDrawing()`, `stampText(...)`.
Clones: `createClone(sprite?)`, `deleteClone()`, `cloneCount(sprite)`, `currentCloneIndex()` (0 in the original).

## Sensing and values

`keyPressed(key)`, `mouseX()`, `mouseY()`, `timerValue()`, `timerStart()`, `timeNow(unit)`, `touching(sprite, target)`, `distanceTo(target)`, `xOf(sprite)`, `styleOf(sprite)`, `randInt(min, max)`.
Named variables and lists (useful across sprites or for editor-visible data): `setVar(name, v)`, `changeVar(name, d)`, `getVar(name)`, `appendList(name, v)`, `getList(name)`, `listItem(name, mode, index)`, `listLength(name)`. Plain TS variables are usually simpler.
Custom blocks: `defineProc(name, params, body)`, `defineReporter(name, params, body)` — or just write functions.

## Tests

```ts
test("bonus", () => { expect(bonus(3)).toBe(30); });
```
